lessons.title: Desired state
lessons.summary: The desired state of managed infrastructure.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Providers translate resource operations into service API calls.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A resource was edited manually and differs from configuration. Review the plan for drift before applying changes.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It is only a sequential shell script. This is not a sound assumption; the desired state of managed infrastructure.

lessons.takeaway: Providers translate resource operations into service API calls.

lessons.title: Initialization
lessons.summary: Initialize the working directory and required dependencies.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Backend changes may require explicit migration decisions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A fresh checkout cannot load its provider dependencies. Run initialization with the intended backend configuration.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It applies every planned infrastructure change. This is not a sound assumption; initialize the working directory and required dependencies.

lessons.takeaway: Backend changes may require explicit migration decisions.

lessons.title: Planning
lessons.summary: A proposed set of changes based on configuration and observed state.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A plan is a review opportunity rather than a guarantee against future drift.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A plan unexpectedly proposes replacing a database. Inspect the replacement cause and data-protection strategy.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It necessarily performs every proposed change. This is not a sound assumption; a proposed set of changes based on configuration and observed state.

lessons.takeaway: A plan is a review opportunity rather than a guarantee against future drift.

lessons.title: State mapping
lessons.summary: To map configuration addresses to managed remote objects.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: State is operational data that requires protection and recovery planning.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A resource exists remotely but its state mapping is missing. Investigate the mapping and consider a controlled import.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: State is merely optional console formatting. This is not a sound assumption; to map configuration addresses to managed remote objects.

lessons.takeaway: State is operational data that requires protection and recovery planning.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.summary: Parameters for a Terraform module.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Types and validation can catch invalid inputs early.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A module receives an invalid environment name. Add explicit input validation and clear accepted values.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Variables automatically encrypt every value. This is not a sound assumption; parameters for a Terraform module.

lessons.takeaway: Types and validation can catch invalid inputs early.

lessons.title: Outputs
lessons.summary: Expose selected values from a module.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Outputs can contain sensitive data and need appropriate handling.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A pipeline prints a credential-bearing output into shared logs. Mark and handle sensitive values appropriately and restrict log exposure.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Outputs are never stored with state. This is not a sound assumption; expose selected values from a module.

lessons.takeaway: Outputs can contain sensitive data and need appropriate handling.

lessons.title: Providers
lessons.summary: A plugin implementing interactions with a service or platform.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Provider versions affect resource behavior and schema.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An upgrade changes a resource's planned behavior. Review provider version changes and test the plan.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A provider is the same thing as a variable file. This is not a sound assumption; a plugin implementing interactions with a service or platform.

lessons.takeaway: Provider versions affect resource behavior and schema.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.summary: A reusable group of Terraform configuration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A clear module interface reduces coupling to implementation details.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Teams duplicate similar infrastructure with inconsistent defaults. Create a versioned module with deliberate inputs and outputs.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A module is a separate cloud account by definition. This is not a sound assumption; a reusable group of Terraform configuration.

lessons.takeaway: A clear module interface reduces coupling to implementation details.

lessons.title: Lock files
lessons.summary: Selected provider versions and checksums.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Commit the lock file to support consistent provider selection.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two CI runs install different provider builds after initialization. Review constraints and commit the intended provider lock selections.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It locks all remote infrastructure against edits. This is not a sound assumption; selected provider versions and checksums.

lessons.takeaway: Commit the lock file to support consistent provider selection.

lessons.title: Remote state
lessons.summary: It centralizes state access and can support collaboration controls.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Backend locking capability depends on the chosen backend.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two engineers apply against separate local state copies. Move to a coordinated backend with appropriate access and locking.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Remote storage makes all state contents non-sensitive. This is not a sound assumption; it centralizes state access and can support collaboration controls.

lessons.takeaway: Backend locking capability depends on the chosen backend.

lessons.title: State locking
lessons.summary: Concurrent writers corrupting the same state workflow.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A lock should be cleared only after verifying its owner is inactive.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An apply is blocked by a lock after a runner interruption. Verify the original operation stopped before a controlled unlock.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Locking prevents every manual cloud-console edit. This is not a sound assumption; concurrent writers corrupting the same state workflow.

lessons.takeaway: A lock should be cleared only after verifying its owner is inactive.

lessons.title: Sensitive values
lessons.summary: Redact it from ordinary user-facing output.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Sensitive marking alone does not encrypt stored state.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A team commits state believing sensitive values were removed. Restrict and remediate exposure and secure the state storage.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It removes every occurrence from state automatically. This is not a sound assumption; redact it from ordinary user-facing output.

lessons.takeaway: Sensitive marking alone does not encrypt stored state.

lessons.title: Resource addresses
lessons.summary: Keys form part of resource instance identity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Changing a key can appear as removal and creation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Renaming a map key proposes destroying a live object. Review address migration and use an appropriate moved mapping.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Keys only affect display order. This is not a sound assumption; keys form part of resource instance identity.

lessons.takeaway: Changing a key can appear as removal and creation.

lessons.title: Count indexing
lessons.summary: Later numeric indices can shift their resource associations.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Stable semantic keys can reduce unintended identity changes.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Removing the first subnet name causes several unexpected changes. Review index shifts and migrate toward stable keys where appropriate.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Count indices are permanently tied to object names. This is not a sound assumption; later numeric indices can shift their resource associations.

lessons.takeaway: Stable semantic keys can reduce unintended identity changes.

lessons.title: Dependencies
lessons.summary: References between resource values form graph edges.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Explicit depends_on is for dependencies not represented by normal references.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A resource requires a hidden prerequisite not expressed by an input reference. Represent the dependency explicitly and explain why it is needed.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: File ordering determines every resource execution order. This is not a sound assumption; references between resource values form graph edges.

lessons.takeaway: Explicit depends_on is for dependencies not represented by normal references.

lessons.title: Data sources
lessons.summary: Read information about objects or service data.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Reading an object is different from declaring ownership of its lifecycle.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A module needs an existing network identifier without managing that network. Use an appropriate data lookup or explicit input.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every data source creates the referenced object. This is not a sound assumption; read information about objects or service data.

lessons.takeaway: Reading an object is different from declaring ownership of its lifecycle.

lessons.title: Import
lessons.summary: A mapping from an existing remote object to a resource address.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Configuration still needs to match intended management behavior.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A manually created database must become managed infrastructure. Prepare configuration import the object and review the resulting plan.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Import guarantees a subsequent plan has no changes. This is not a sound assumption; a mapping from an existing remote object to a resource address.

lessons.takeaway: Configuration still needs to match intended management behavior.

lessons.title: Moved blocks
lessons.summary: An intentional resource address change.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Address migration can preserve an existing object's identity.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A refactor moves a resource into a child module. Describe the address move and verify the plan avoids unintended replacement.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It automatically copies data between unrelated databases. This is not a sound assumption; an intentional resource address change.

lessons.takeaway: Address migration can preserve an existing object's identity.

lessons.title: Lifecycle protection
lessons.summary: It is a configuration safeguard rather than universal deletion protection.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Remote authorization and backups remain necessary.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A critical database has prevent_destroy but administrators can delete it externally. Add appropriate service-level protection and recovery controls.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It prevents deletion through every external API. This is not a sound assumption; it is a configuration safeguard rather than universal deletion protection.

lessons.takeaway: Remote authorization and backups remain necessary.

lessons.title: Ignored changes
lessons.summary: It delegates selected differences away from normal reconciliation.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Broad ignores can hide meaningful configuration drift.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A broad lifecycle ignore hides an unexpected security setting change. Narrow the ignored attributes and review ownership boundaries.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It makes ignored attributes immutable in the remote service. This is not a sound assumption; it delegates selected differences away from normal reconciliation.

lessons.takeaway: Broad ignores can hide meaningful configuration drift.

lessons.title: Replacement order
lessons.summary: Create a replacement before destroying the old object.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Name uniqueness quotas and dependency behavior can limit this approach.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A replacement cannot coexist because the service requires a unique fixed name. Review naming capacity and migration constraints.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It guarantees zero downtime for every resource. This is not a sound assumption; create a replacement before destroying the old object.

lessons.takeaway: Name uniqueness quotas and dependency behavior can limit this approach.

lessons.title: Targeted applies
lessons.summary: Targeting can leave the overall configuration only partially reconciled.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Exceptional targeted work should be followed by a full plan review.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An emergency targeted apply completes. Run a full plan to inspect remaining differences.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Targeting always applies every dependent change in the whole configuration. This is not a sound assumption; targeting can leave the overall configuration only partially reconciled.

lessons.takeaway: Exceptional targeted work should be followed by a full plan review.

lessons.title: Provisioners
lessons.summary: Native resources model lifecycle and changes more explicitly.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Provisioners can introduce imperative side effects that are harder to track.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A shell provisioner leaves partially configured hosts on failure. Use image or configuration tooling and explicit lifecycle ownership.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Provisioners make every shell command idempotent. This is not a sound assumption; native resources model lifecycle and changes more explicitly.

lessons.takeaway: Provisioners can introduce imperative side effects that are harder to track.

lessons.title: Workspace boundaries
lessons.summary: They separate state instances but do not inherently isolate credentials or permissions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Strong environment isolation may need separate backends and access boundaries.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A developer workspace can still authenticate with production-wide credentials. Separate access controls and backend boundaries according to risk.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Each workspace automatically creates a new cloud account. This is not a sound assumption; they separate state instances but do not inherently isolate credentials or permissions.

lessons.takeaway: Strong environment isolation may need separate backends and access boundaries.

lessons.title: Saved plans
lessons.summary: It can contain sensitive configuration and state information.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Apply should use the reviewed artifact under controlled conditions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A pipeline uploads a plan artifact to a public location. Restrict artifact access and handle potential secret exposure.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Plan files contain no secrets by design. This is not a sound assumption; it can contain sensitive configuration and state information.

lessons.takeaway: Apply should use the reviewed artifact under controlled conditions.

lessons.title: Drift policy
lessons.summary: Decide whether to adopt or revert the change based on intent.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Blind reconciliation can undo an emergency fix.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An emergency firewall rule differs from versioned configuration. Review the reason and reconcile configuration deliberately.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: All manual changes must be reverted without investigation. This is not a sound assumption; decide whether to adopt or revert the change based on intent.

lessons.takeaway: Blind reconciliation can undo an emergency fix.

lessons.title: State splitting
lessons.summary: Reduce coupling access scope and change blast radius.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Cross-state dependencies need explicit interface and sequencing decisions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A small application change routinely locks a huge shared stack. Evaluate boundaries by lifecycle ownership and risk.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: More state files automatically remove all dependencies. This is not a sound assumption; reduce coupling access scope and change blast radius.

lessons.takeaway: Cross-state dependencies need explicit interface and sequencing decisions.

lessons.title: Partial failure
lessons.summary: Some resources may have changed successfully before failure.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The next step is to inspect state and actual resources before retrying.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An apply fails halfway through a network rollout. Inspect completed changes and review a fresh plan.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every failed apply automatically rolls back all changes. This is not a sound assumption; some resources may have changed successfully before failure.

lessons.takeaway: The next step is to inspect state and actual resources before retrying.

lessons.title: Provider upgrades
lessons.summary: Review migration guidance and plans in a representative environment.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Schema changes may affect existing resources without configuration edits.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A new provider version proposes unexpected replacements. Investigate release changes and test a controlled migration.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A major version change can never affect resource behavior. This is not a sound assumption; review migration guidance and plans in a representative environment.

lessons.takeaway: Schema changes may affect existing resources without configuration edits.

lessons.title: Policy checks
lessons.summary: Reject changes that violate defined infrastructure rules.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Policy checks complement plan review rather than proving all runtime behavior.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A plan opens a sensitive service to the Internet. Block the unsafe exposure and explain the required exception process.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Passing policy guarantees no outage can occur. This is not a sound assumption; reject changes that violate defined infrastructure rules.

lessons.takeaway: Policy checks complement plan review rather than proving all runtime behavior.
